name: Quinta da Regaleira
seoTitle: Quinta da Regaleira: Initiation Well, Queues and Timing
tagline: Sintra's garden of wells, grottoes and tunnels, the easier Sintra option from the ship

description.short: An early 20th-century estate on the edge of Sintra's historic centre, known for its Initiation Well, tunnels and symbolic gardens. It is the Sintra sight closest to the train station, but still 75 to 90 minutes each way from the cruise terminal.
description.full:
Regaleira is the more manageable of the two famous Sintra sights for a cruise passenger, because it sits at the edge of Sintra town rather than on top of the hill. It is still a long trip: 75 to 90 minutes each way from the Jardim do Tabaco terminal by metro to Restauradores, train from Rossio to Sintra (about 40 minutes) and then a 20 to 25-minute walk through the historic centre, or Scotturb bus 435. With two hours on site and a safety margin, it needs a call of about seven to eight hours at the very least.

Entry is by timed slot every 30 minutes, and the ticket is valid only for the date and time printed on it, with up to one hour's tolerance for late arrival. Buy it on the official online ticket office before you sail; the estate has warned about tickets bought through unofficial sites.

The garden, not the house, is the reason to come. Only the main floor of the palace is open. Head first for the Initiation Well, a spiral stairway of about 27 m that you walk down to a tunnel at the bottom, because a queue forms there by late morning. From the bottom, the tunnels lead out to the lake and grottoes. The paths are steep, uneven and often damp, so shoes with grip matter more than usual.

If you have limited time, do the well, the tunnels, the lake, the chapel and a quick look at the palace, and skip the upper viewpoints. Crowds are heaviest between late morning and mid-afternoon. The estate's small aquarium feature is currently closed for restoration.
description.history: In 1892 the estate was bought by António Augusto Carvalho Monteiro, a wealthy collector born in Brazil and known in Lisbon as "Monteiro dos Milhões". Between about 1904 and 1910 the Italian architect and stage designer Luigi Manini built the palace, chapel and gardens for him. Manini's background in theatre shows: the garden is designed as a sequence of scenes. Its symbolism draws on Dante, Camões, alchemy, the Templars and freemasonry, although Carvalho Monteiro never explained his intentions in writing, which is why interpretations vary.
description.significance: Regaleira shows a different side of Sintra from Pena: a private, intellectual fantasy rather than a royal residence. The Initiation Well has become one of the most recognisable images of Portugal. For a cruise passenger, it is the single Sintra sight that can be reached on foot from the train station and seen properly in about two hours.

directions.general: Located in Sintra historic town center, walking distance from Sintra National Palace and train station. Entrance on Rua Barbosa du Bocage.
directions.fromCruisePort: Walk about 10 minutes to Santa Apolónia and take the metro Blue Line to Restauradores; Rossio station is a two-minute walk. Trains from Rossio reach Sintra in about 40 minutes. From Sintra station walk 20 to 25 minutes through the historic centre, or take Scotturb bus 435. Allow 75 to 90 minutes door to door each way.
directions.publicTransport: Train from Lisbon Rossio to Sintra station (40 min). Then 10-minute walk through historic center. Well signposted from station.
directions.parking: Limited street parking near entrance. Public parking in Sintra town center (5-10 minute walk). Parking fills quickly - arrive early or use public transport.

distanceFromCruisePort.drivingTime: 40-50 minutes by car, 60-90 minutes by public transport

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open daily except 1 January and 24, 25 and 31 December

seasonal.hours: 09:00 - 19:30 (palace and chapel 10:00 - 19:00 from 10 August to 30 September 2026)

admissionPrices.notes: 2026 prices: adults 18-64 20 euros, youths 6-17 15 euros, seniors 65+ 15 euros, children up to 5 free, family (2 adults or seniors + 2 youths) 60 euros. Visitors with a disability and one companion: 12 euros each. Audioguide 5 euros, on site only. Timed entry; tickets valid only for the date and slot shown.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: The earliest slots of the day, before the well queue builds. Weekdays outside summer are quieter.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Buy timed tickets on the official online ticket office. Visit the Initiation Well first. Wear shoes with grip for damp steps and tunnels. Only the palace's main floor is open. Last entry 17:30.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 5 to 5.5 hours door to door (75-90 minutes each way plus about 2 hours on site); needs a call of 7-8 hours or more
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Metro and a 40-minute train, then a 20-25 minute walk or short bus ride. On site, paths are steep and uneven, and the Initiation Well and tunnels involve many steps; not suitable for wheelchairs.
tips: Buy a timed ticket on the official online ticket office (regaleira.byblueticket.pt) before you sail; the estate warns against unofficial resellers.
Tickets are valid for their date and slot, with up to one hour's tolerance for late arrival: pick a slot that allows for the train.
Go to the Initiation Well first; the queue there grows from late morning.
The tunnels are dark and wet in places; shoes with grip and a phone torch help.
Only the palace's main floor is open, so do not budget much time for the interior.
Adults pay 20 euros, youths 6-17 and seniors 65+ pay 15 euros, children up to 5 go free.
The last entry is 17:30 all year, earlier than the garden's closing time.
Closed on 1 January and 24, 25 and 31 December.

highlights: Initiation Well, a spiral stairway of about 27 m descending into the ground
Unfinished Well, a smaller rough-stone shaft
Tunnels and grottoes linking the wells to the lake
Neo-Manueline palace, main floor open to visitors
Chapel of the Holy Trinity with symbolic decoration
Terraces and towers with views over Sintra
facilities: Timed online tickets through the official ticket office
Audioguide rental (5 euros, includes map; on-site only)
Printed map (0.50 euros) or free downloadable map
Restrooms, including new facilities near the greenhouse

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Very limited wheelchair accessibility. Gardens feature steep staircases, narrow underground tunnels, uneven paths, and the famous Initiation Well requires descending 9 levels of spiral stairs. Palace interior has multiple floors with no elevator. Visitors with mobility limitations can access limited ground-level garden areas but will miss majority of main attractions. Contact in advance for accessible route information.
accessibility.visualAidServices: Audio guide app with detailed descriptions; guided tours can accommodate visually impaired with advance notice
accessibility.hearingAidServices: Visual information displays; self-guided exploration possible without audio
